page: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 8), table 'Campus Financial Facts: Berkeley - Merced Campuses (in thousands of dollars)'
differences_from_original: None in the amounts: both component lines, both sums, the combined total, the page and the IPEDS match agree with the first researcher's record. note: The table is printed in thousands of dollars; amounts here are multiplied by 1,000 to whole dollars. The table prints component lines only, so every total is the verifier's addition. The table's own heading for the Regents-held lines is 'University endowments' (the audited Note 17, PDF p. 100, describes these as endowments 'held and administered by the University'); it does not use the words 'held by The Regents'. A third line printed under 'University endowments', 'Annual income distribution', is a yearly payout, not a balance, and is left out of the total (the eleven columns sum to 600,614 thousand, which agrees with the audited Note 17 statement that $600.6 million was transferred to the campuses, PDF p. 101). Cross-checks against the audited pages of the same report, all in thousands: the 'Nonspendable endowments' line summed over the ten campuses and Systemwide is 1,316,568, equal to the audited 'Restricted: Nonexpendable: Endowments and gifts' (PDF p. 34) and Table 17.1a (PDF p. 100). The other lines do not tie exactly: University 'Nonspendable' plus 'Other' over all columns is 19,242,993 against audited endowments 6,306,367 plus funds functioning as endowments 14,000,115 = 20,306,482 (difference 1,063,489, not explained in the report); campus foundations' two lines over ten campuses are 13,458,374 against audited Table 17.2a endowments 10,394,411 plus funds functioning as endowments 3,084,513 = 13,478,924 (difference 20,550; the audited figure covers 11 foundations including the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory foundation, PDF p. 40, while the table has ten campus columns, but the report does not say that this is the reason). The audited statements give no endowment figure by campus. The same table, with identical figures, is in the copy filed with the Regents' November 2024 meeting (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/regmeet/nov24/c2attach2.pdf). For the double-counting check this verifier read the audited statements of the U.C. San Diego, UC Riverside and UC Santa Barbara foundations (see overlap_note); each ties to the foundation total. The UC Davis Foundation, UC Berkeley Foundation and UC Irvine Foundation sites returned HTTP 403 to this verifier, and The UCLA Foundation's statements were not located.
overlap_note: PLAIN ANSWER: these are two separate pools owned by two separate legal entities, and adding the table's 'University endowments' lines to its 'Campus foundations' endowments' lines does not count any money twice. Audited UC Annual Financial Report 2023-24, Note 1, PDF p. 40: 'The University has 11 legally separate, tax-exempt, affiliated foundations, one for each campus and the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL). The economic resources received or held by the foundations are entirely for the benefit of the campuses ... the campus foundations are reported under GASB requirements as discretely presented component units of the University.' Note 17, PDF p. 100: 'Endowments and gifts are held and administered either by the University or by the campus foundations.' PDF p. 101: endowments 'held by the campus foundations and administered by each of their independent Boards of Trustees'. Note 21, PDF p. 106: 'Although independent boards govern these foundations, their assets are dedicated for the benefit of the University of California.' (2) FOUNDATION MONEY PLACED IN THE REGENTS' POOLS is counted in the foundation's column only. Audited Note 3, PDF p. 59: 'The campus foundations' cash and cash equivalents and investments that are invested with the University are excluded from the University's statements of net position and included in the campus foundations' statements of net position.' Note 1, PDF p. 42: 'the campus foundations' investments in University-managed investment pools and their allocated share of the securities lending activities have been excluded from the University's financial statements and included in the Campus Foundations' columns.' Table 3.7a, PDF p. 58, deducts 'Campus foundations' investments with the University (3,673,607)' thousand (of which GEP 3,024,147) in arriving at the University's total investments. The unaudited campus table itself is silent: its only footnotes concern 'Other' operating expenses and the Systemwide column. That it follows the audited treatment is an inference, supported by its 'Nonspendable endowments' line summing to the audited net-position figure (1,316,568 thousand). (3) COMBINED TOTALS IN OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS. The UC annual report prints no combined Regents-plus-foundation endowment figure, per campus or system-wide. The UC Annual Endowment Report, fiscal year ended June 30, 2024 (prepared by Mercer Investments, LLC for UC Investments; unaudited market values; https://www.ucop.edu/investment-office/investment-reports/annual-reports/annual-endwoment-report-fy-2023-2024.pdf), section 3.2 'Total University Endowed Assets', PDF p. 7, does print 'Total Endowment Assets' per campus and system-wide ($41,146,002 thousand for all campuses and systemwide programs: Regents 26,485,499; Foundation investments in GEP 2,942,813, in BGP 490, in STIP 70,862; Foundation 11,646,338). Its columns are mutually exclusive by footnote: '1 Assets managed by Regents in GEP and BGP for the benefit of the campuses excluding investment allocations to the GEP, BGP and STIP by the campus Foundations'; '2 Foundation endowment assets invested in GEP, BGP, and STIP provided by campus Foundations'; '3 Assets managed by the campus Foundations excluding investment allocations to the GEP, BGP and STIP'. Each printed total equals the sum of that report's own five columns (to within 1 thousand of rounding), so that report does not double count either. Its totals do NOT equal the simple sum of the annual report's two columns, because it is on a different basis: market value of everything UC Investments manages for the campus in the General Endowment Pool and the Blue & Gold Pool, and the audited annual report (PDF p. 49) describes the Blue & Gold Pool as a vehicle 'to invest long-term excess reserves', which is wider than endowment. WHERE DOUBLE COUNTING WOULD ARISE: only by mixing bases, for example adding a foundation's endowment to the whole General Endowment Pool, whose total 'include[s] Regents Investment in GEP, Foundation Investment in GEP, and Other Foundation and Affiliate Investments in GEP' (Endowment Report, PDF p. 6, footnote 1). THIS CAMPUS, Endowment Report PDF p. 7, row 'Berkeley', $ thousands: Regents 5,768,629; Foundation investments in GEP 0, in BGP 0, in STIP 16,169; Foundation 3,096,139; printed Total Endowment Assets 8,880,937 (the five columns add to 8,880,937). The four foundation columns add to 3,112,308 against 3,176,106 in the annual report table. The annual report table's two groups add to 8,046,236, which differs from the Endowment Report's printed 8,880,937 by 834,701; the two documents are not on the same basis and should not be mixed.
